approved: Export Control Amendment (Clarifying Obligations Relating to Registered Establishments) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would reduce the regulatory burden on Australia's export industry by clarifying obligations for registered establishments under the Export Control Act 2020.

It would allow export operations to occur at registered establishments without being listed in the registration when not required as a condition of export, and expand the types of export documents the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry can issue to include non-consignment-specific certificates requested by trading partners.

The changes are part of a broader export assurance reform project that will eventually prescribe certain goods like wool, rendered products, skins and hides, animal food, honey and bee products, and pharmaceuticals as 'general products' under the Act.
Allow export operations at registered establishments without registration coverage when not a prescribed export condition.
Expand the range of export documentation issuable by the department to include certificates not tied to a specific consignment.
Reduce the scope of the offence under section 143 so operators are only penalised if they fail to meet prescribed export conditions.
Industry stakeholders involved in exporting general products such as wool, rendered goods, skins, hides, animal food, honey, bee products, food, beverages, and pharmaceuticals.

Ordered that the Export Control Amendment (Clarifying Obligations Relating to Registered Establishments) Bill 2026 and the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No. 1) Bill 2026 be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration after debate on each second-reading motion is adjourned.

Supported the Export Control Amendment (Clarifying Obligations Relating to Registered Establishments) Bill 2026, which would reduce regulatory burdens and broaden export documentation powers; the response said it would support export assurance reform, and the bill was read a second time.

Moved that government business, including five specified bills and a related bill subject to introduction, be considered from 12.15 pm until no later than 1.30 pm, followed by general business notice of motion no. 510 concerning the 2026-27 Budget. The question was agreed to.

Announced coalition support for the Export Control Amendment (Clarifying Obligations Relating to Registered Establishments) Bill 2026, describing measures to reduce regulatory burden and expand export documentation; also criticised export cost recovery increases of 47 per cent between 2020 and 2025 and called for them to be abandoned. The bill was read a second time.
